21. The head lines roughly translated, stated that "the LLB certificate of a Judge of the High Court Division is forged?” In the body of the article it is reported that there is a sensational allegation that the LLB degree certificate of an Additional Judge of the High Court Division was forged. The reporter further reported that on inquiry it was  revealed that Justice Faisal Mahmud Faizee (herein after referred as Justice Faizee) took part in the preliminary. and final examination of LLB in 1989 from Chittagong . Law College affiliated to Chittagong University. In the tabulation sheet of the preliminary examination his marks for Muslim Law was shown as 39 at page 60 of the tabulation sheet. The left hand figure (presently shown as 3) is clearly seen to have been tampered with and, there is a red mark underneath the mark for the subject in which he was unsuccessful. The red mark is put on the tabulation sheet by those who prepared it. The pass mark for Muslim Law is 30 and the mark shown against Justice Faizee's name for Muslim Law was shown as 39 with a red mark below it. The reporter went on to say that the staff and officers of the Controller of Examination of Chittagong University indulged in corruption and altered results of examination. As a result of the allegations the University Syndicate set up a three member inquiry committee on 24-4-1996. In due course the Committee examined results of the LLB Examination for the years 1986 to 1992 and found irregularities in respect of 111 examinees for the year 1989. Only the candidate bearing roll No. 3652 (which is the roll number for the final LLB examination of Justice Faizee) is found to contain interpolation. It is further reported that the interpolation of the tabulation sheet does not bear any initial below it. As a result on page 8 of the tabulation sheets the name and roll number of Justice Faizee was marked with a red mark and his result was directed to be withheld. In 350th Syndicate Meeting held on 13th of August, 1999 it was decided to amend the gazette notification relating to the result published and to maintain result of those who were successful, and to cancel the details of the result of those who were unsuccessful. But even after elapse of 5 years the authority concerned did not take any final decision in this matter and held up the result of the concerned candidates and did not hand over their original certificates. The reporter concerned has stated the outcome of his query regarding this matter to persons involved in the Syndicate Meeting. He reported that in answer to a question the Chairman of the 350th Syndicate meeting, Professor Abdul Mannan told him inter-alia that the judiciary is the final shelter place for the citizens and if there is such an occurrence (interpolation of tabulation sheet) then the people will lose their faith. Finally, the reporter also mentioned that a number of persons were involved in the forgery at Chittagong University, including the Controller of Examination. The Controller of Examination had been dismissed and others were given compulsory retirement. Some litigation is pending in this regard. 

 25. The appellants in this case are Reporters, Editors and Publishers of two well known Bengali Daily Newspapers in this country. Naturally the defence is one of freedom of speech as afforded by the constitution. In the present case, essentially the appellants claimed that the matters reported in the newspapers, which are now under scrutiny, relate to inquiry regarding corruption, forgery and interpolation of information contained in tabulation sheets of examinations shed by Chittagong University. The appellants claimed that the matter under investigation being of crucial importance involving persons who are at the helm of this country are liable to be reported openly to the public for their information. According to them the reports simply reflected the findings of inquiry which exposed interpolation in the marks contained in the tabulation sheets as well as the irregularities therein, and that it has been fairly reported that Justice Faizee is one of hundreds whose results are under investigation. In this regard the High Court Division observed that if the newspapers had published only the findings of the inquiry in question, that would not have been contempt. It was further observed that if a Judge commits a crime any news of such action will not be con- tempt since no one is above the law. It was observed that freedom of press is an essential requisite for successful working of democratic institutions, but that freedom should not be abused. In the case of Md. Riaz Uddin Khan vs Mahmudur Rahman reported in 63 DLR (AD) 29, SK Sinha, J quoted Cornelius CJ in Sir Edward Snelson vs Judges, High Court of West Pakistan, Lahore 16 DLR (AD) 535, as follows: 

 27. Let us consider what each of the news papers have reported and the impact that it has had on the judiciary. We note that the report in the daily 'Prothom Alo' appeared on 30 of October, 2004 and the report in the daily 'Bhorer Kagoj' also appeared on the same date. It would be difficult to assess, therefore, which of the two reports, it at all, had the most damaging effect on the reputation of the judiciary in the eyes of the public. We must bear in mind that the public crave for information and hence the development of the media. The public are certainly entitled to receive information regarding all aspects of everyday life which affect them, be it in relation to commerce, industry, foreign affairs, the justice system, social and cultural life in the country etc. To that extent the incidents of forgery, interpolation, manipulation etc. of examination results in Chittagong University or any other educational institutions is of relevance and importance to the public. Hence, reporting such matters, in particular after due inquiry into allegations of irregularity cannot be questioned or denied. When considering the reporting of such issues, it is important to visualize in intention of the reporter, whether it is to truly inform the public by direct and accurate reporting of facts which are matter of record or to sensationalize the subject matter and contents in order to excite the mind of the public. It is true that reporting of any event, occurrence or incident is likely to excite the mind, but if the adding an explanation or comment in the reporting is such that it creates a negative impact and it is the intention of the writer to do so, then his motives become questionable. 

 28. We have noted already that the High Court Division observed that the headlines and headings are not substantiated by materials within the report. We are in total agreement with that. At the same time, we feel that it would be unfortunate if the public would be unduly impressed by simply reading the headlines or headings in a newspaper. The headlines and headings should not by themselves be sufficient to create any effect on the minds of the citizen. A knowledgeable citizen would also read the contents of the report to find out the factual aspects. Upon scrutiny of the materials contained in the report of the 'Prothom Alo', we note that essentially the report is with regard to the incidents of interpolation, forgery etc of results as depicted in the tabulation sheets kept in the office of the Controller of Examination of Chittagong University. In our view such a report most certainly creates an impression of malpractice within that office of Chittagong University. That newspaper has given a description about the interpolation detected against the name and, roll number of Justice Faizee. In that report we do not find any personal view of the reporter as to the effect that has or had on the judiciary. 

 29. On the other hand, we note from the report appearing in the 'Bhorer Kagoj' that the reporter has gone into matters which are extraneous to the issue of interpolation of marks in the tabulation sheet, e.g. when he referred to Justice Faizee being the nephew of a Member of Parliament, who had lost his position as a Minister because of his failure to keep price of commodities under control Inclusion of such information in this report clearly shows coloring by the reporter which is ultimately used to paint the character of Justice Faizee, which has been highlighted by the High Court Division noting that Justice Faizee was "আলোচিত বিচারপতি, বিতর্কিত বিচারপতি" and "এল এল বি পাশ না করেই বিচারপতি!" The reporter also added comments alleged to have been made by an unnamed former Vice-Chancellor that if such a corrupt person is appointed as a Judge or engaged in the law profession then what is the future of our society? He went on to say, apparently reporting what the former Vice-Chancellor said, that if corrupt persons are appointed as Judges of the highest Court then the present and future will both be thrust into darkness. In our view such expressions of the reporter are motivated to and in fact do excite disaffection and rouse dissatisfaction in the minds of the people with regard to the justice delivery system. 

 31. In the light of the above, it is our opinion that the news report published in the daily 'Bhorer Kagoj' , impugned before the High Court Division, certainly had the effect of scandalizing the justice delivery system. However, upon careful, scrutiny of the full reports we are inclined to accept that the report in the daily 'Prothom Alo' does not by itself have the effect of scandalizing the concerned Judge or the judiciary. What the report does, in fact, is bring into focus scandals involved in the tabulation sheets of examination marks by the Chittagong University. However, the report by the 'Bhorer Kagoj' goes further than a simple narration of the inquiry and findings with regard to the manipulation of marks in the tabulation sheets by the office of the Controller of Examination of Chittagong University and gives the personal opinion of the reporter as to what effect the corruption, forgery, interpolation etc. brings upon the judiciary when such persons whose examination results are manipulated are appointed as Judges of the Supreme Court. This would clearly have a negative effect on the minds of the general public and undermine their confidence in the justice delivery system.
